component.name: Devmode
component.summary: Manage repos and group them into workspaces

description.p: Devmode is a project management utility for developers. It helps you manage repositories and group them into workspaces.

ul.li: Track repos you clone, create, or already have on disk in a local registry.
Lay out cloned repos automatically under a configurable root.
Group repos into workspaces with their own editor and environment.
Open every repo in a workspace with a single command.

description.p: First public release, and a ground-up rewrite. Devmode now ships a desktop app, a terminal UI, and the dm command line tool, all sharing one local registry.

ul.li: Track repositories you clone, create, or already have on disk in a local registry.
Lay cloned repositories out automatically under a configurable root, with built-in or custom naming conventions.
Group repositories into non-destructive workspaces, each with its own default editor and environment variables.
Open every repository in a workspace at once.
Discover untracked repositories on disk and reconcile entries that no longer match reality.

description.p: Maintenance release focused on trimming the tool down.

ul.li: Separated the command line interface from the shared core logic.
Reworked workspaces to be easier to use.
Removed most subcommands and several configuration options.
Improved dependency usage and internal error handling.
Create, rename, and delete workspaces.
Clone a repository directly into a workspace.
Add existing repositories to a workspace and remove them again.

description.p: Published to crates.io as dm, with a shorter command name.

ul.li: Added the fork command: clone a repository and set its upstream to your fork.
Clone several repositories in one invocation, including private ones.
Added short aliases for the subcommands.
Rebuilt the configuration handling with integrity checks for a missing or corrupt config directory.

description.p: First release of the devmode command line tool.

ul.li: Clone repositories into a consistent host/owner/repository folder structure.
Open a tracked project in your configured text editor.
Configure your text editor, Git host, and Git user.
